label: Selachians are internally oviparous but bring forth live young
claim: The cartilaginous fishes form an egg inside the uterus but give birth to live young; their egg is soft-shelled and of one colour.
quote: The cartilaginous fishes, as has been often said already, are oviparous internally but produce the young alive, the egg changing previously from one part of the uterus to another; and their egg is soft-shelled and of one colour.
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode (aplacental/placental viviparity vs oviparity) across chondrichthyan species
egg-case/egg-shell consistency
candidate_data: Reproductive-mode compilations for elasmobranchs in FishBase and the published comparative literature on chondrichthyan reproduction.

label: Wind-eggs occur in heavy, prolific birds, not in birds of prey
claim: Unfertilised 'wind-eggs' are produced by birds that are not strong fliers or predators and that produce many young, not by birds of prey.
quote: Some embryos are formed in birds spontaneously, which are called wind-eggs and ‘zephyria’ by some; these occur in birds which are not given to flight nor rapine but which produce many young
scope: birds: fowls, partridges, pigeons contrasted with birds of prey
measurable_quantities: occurrence of unfertilised egg-laying by unmated females across bird orders
clutch size
flight style / predatory habit
candidate_data: Clutch-size and life-history data in the Amniote Life-History Database and AVONET; poultry and raptor husbandry records of laying by unmated females.

label: Birds of prey lay few eggs because residual matter goes to wings
claim: Because both wings and semen are made from the same residual matter, birds whose residue goes into wings and feathers (birds of prey) mate little and lay few eggs.
quote: Since then both the wings and the semen are made from residual matter, nature cannot afford to spend much upon both. And for this same reason the birds of prey are neither given to treading much nor to laying many eggs
scope: birds, especially birds of prey versus heavy ground birds
measurable_quantities: clutch size versus wing loading or flight investment across bird species
copulation frequency
candidate_data: AVONET morphometrics (wing shape, mass) combined with clutch sizes from the Amniote Life-History Database.

label: The cuckoo lays few eggs and lays them in other birds' nests
claim: The cuckoo, though not a bird of prey, lays few eggs, and it lays them in the nests of other birds; Aristotle attributes this to its cold, cowardly nature.
quote: The cuckoo, though not a bird of prey, lays few eggs, because it is of a cold nature, as is shown by the cowardice of the bird, whereas a generative animal should be hot and moist. That it is cowardly is plain, for it is pursued by all the birds and lays eggs in the nests of others.
measurable_quantities: eggs laid per female per season
frequency of brood parasitism
mobbing of cuckoos by other birds
candidate_data: Breeding biology of Cuculus canorus in the Animal Diversity Web and the Amniote Life-History Database; brood-parasitism field studies.

label: The lioness bears five or six cubs, then fewer each year, then none
claim: A lioness produces five or six cubs at her first birth, four the next year, then three, and so down to one and finally none, as her generative secretion is used up with age.
quote: A similar condition is the cause of the later sterility of the lioness, for at the first birth she produces five or six, then in the next year four, and again three cubs, then the next number down to one, then none at all
measurable_quantities: litter size by parity and female age
inter-birth interval
age at reproductive senescence
candidate_data: Long-term lion population studies (e.g. Serengeti Lion Project) and litter-size data in AnAge and PanTHERIA.

label: Wind-eggs arise without any prior impregnation
claim: Unfertilised wind-eggs are not relics of a previous mating: they arise in hens and geese that have never been impregnated.
quote: Hence some are wont to speak of wind-eggs as not coming into being independently but as mere relics from a previous impregnation. But this is a false view, for sufficient observations have been made of their arising without impregnation in chickens and goslings.
measurable_quantities: egg production in females reared without males
candidate_data: Poultry-science records of egg laying in hens and geese kept without males.

label: Fish lay incomplete eggs because they are too numerous to finish inside
claim: Birds lay their eggs complete, whereas externally spawning fish lay incomplete eggs that finish growing outside the mother, because fish produce too many eggs for all to be completed inside her.
quote: Among creatures that lay eggs externally birds produce their egg perfect, fish imperfect, but the eggs of the latter complete their growth outside as has been said before. The reason is that the fish kind is very fertile; now it is impossible for many eggs to reach completion within the mother and therefore they lay them outside.
measurable_quantities: egg size change after spawning (water uptake)
fecundity
developmental state at release
candidate_data: Fecundity and egg-size data in FishBase; avian egg data in the Amniote Life-History Database.

label: Bird eggs are two-coloured, all fish eggs one-coloured
claim: The eggs of birds are two-coloured (white and yolk), while the eggs of all fishes are of one colour.
quote: While the eggs of birds are two-coloured, those of all fish are one-coloured.
measurable_quantities: presence of a separate albumen layer in eggs across birds and fishes
candidate_data: Comparative egg-structure descriptions in developmental biology literature; Phenoscape/Uberon annotations for egg components.

label: Water birds' eggs have larger, paler yolks than land birds' eggs
claim: Lake (water) birds, being moister and colder than land birds, lay eggs whose yolk is larger and less yellow.
quote: This is what we find in lake birds, for they are of a moister nature and are colder than the land birds, so that the so-called ‘lecithus’ or yolk in the eggs of such birds is large and less yellow because the white is less separated off from it.
scope: aquatic (lake) birds such as ducks and geese versus land birds
measurable_quantities: yolk fraction of egg mass
yolk colour
candidate_data: Comparative avian egg-composition data (yolk-to-albumen ratios) from the poultry and avian-egg literature.

label: A hen's egg is laid with the sharp end last
claim: The sharp end of a bird's egg, where it was attached to the uterus, comes out of the hen after the blunt end.
quote: And this is why the sharp end of the egg comes out of the hen later than the blunt end; for the part attached to the uterus comes out later, and the egg is attached at the point where is the said principle, and the principle is in the sharp end.
measurable_quantities: orientation of the egg at oviposition
candidate_data: Poultry physiology observations of egg orientation during oviposition.

label: The eggshell is soft when laid and hardens by cooling
claim: A bird's eggshell is still soft when the egg is laid and hardens immediately afterwards by cooling as its moisture evaporates.
quote: it is not observed that the shell is at first only a soft membrane, and that it is only after the egg is perfected that it becomes hard and brittle; this is so nicely adjusted that it is still soft when it comes out (for otherwise it would cause pain in laying), but no sooner has it come out than it is fixed hard by cooling
measurable_quantities: eggshell hardness at and after oviposition
timing of shell calcification
candidate_data: Avian reproductive physiology on shell-gland calcification in the domestic fowl.

label: Live-bearing selachians keep the young attached to the uterus by an umbilicus
claim: In some cartilaginous fishes the egg stays attached to the uterus, and when the young fish is complete it is still connected to the uterus by an umbilical cord after the yolk is used up, as in the smooth dogfish.
quote: in some of the cartilaginous fish the egg is not detached from the uterus, but is still connected with it as it comes downwards with a view to the production of the young alive; in these the young fish when perfected is still connected by the umbilicus to the uterus when the egg has been consumed.
scope: some selachians, notably the 'smooth hound' (Mustelus, smooth dogfish)
measurable_quantities: presence of a yolk-sac placenta / umbilical connection in late embryos
candidate_data: Reproductive-mode data for Mustelus species in FishBase and the elasmobranch placentation literature.

label: Fish are prolific because most of their eggs are destroyed
claim: Most fish eggs that are laid are destroyed before hatching, and fish produce great numbers of eggs to make up for this loss.
quote: even as it is most of those laid are destroyed before hatching. Hence the class of fish is prolific, for Nature makes up for the destruction by numbers.
measurable_quantities: egg and larval mortality
fecundity
candidate_data: Fecundity data in FishBase and egg/larval mortality estimates from fisheries recruitment studies.

label: All fish have separate sexes except the erythrinus and the channa
claim: In all fishes some individuals have milt organs and others a uterus, except two kinds, the erythrinus and the channa, which have no separate males.
quote: But, as it is, some of them have organs for milt and others have a uterus, and this distinction obtains in all except two, the erythrinus and the channa, some of them having the milt organs, others a uterus.
scope: fishes; erythrinus and channa are probably sea perches (Serranus)
measurable_quantities: gonochorism versus hermaphroditism across fish species
candidate_data: Sexual-system data for fishes in FishBase and published compilations of hermaphroditism in teleosts.

label: Female fish do not conceive by swallowing milt
claim: Fish are not conceived by the female swallowing the male's milt, because the passage from the mouth leads to the intestine, not the uterus.
quote: as if fish were conceived by the mother’s swallowing the milt,— not considering that this is impossible. For the passage which enters by way of the mouth runs to the intestines, not to the uterus
measurable_quantities: route of fertilisation in fishes
anatomical connection between gut and gonoduct
candidate_data: Comparative fish anatomy and reproductive biology (FishBase reproduction fields; Phenoscape anatomy).

label: The hyena has only one kind of genitals, not both sexes
claim: The hyena does not have both male and female genitals; each animal has one, but both sexes have a mark under the tail resembling the female genitals.
quote: This is untrue, for the hyena has been seen to have only one pudendum, there being no lack of opportunity for observation in some districts, but hyenas have under the tail a line like the pudendum of the female.
measurable_quantities: external genital anatomy of male and female hyenas
presence of a subcaudal/anal scent gland
candidate_data: Hyaenid anatomy in the Animal Diversity Web and the mammalogy literature on hyena genitalia and anal pouches.

label: Eggs fertilised by one cock take on the nature of a later cock
claim: Eggs already impregnated by one cock change to the nature of a second cock that treads the hen later, provided this happens before the white separates from the yolk.
quote: In birds the wind-eggs become fertile, and those previously impregnated by one kind of cock change their nature to that of the later cock.
measurable_quantities: paternity of eggs after sequential matings with two males
time interval between matings
candidate_data: Sperm-competition and last-male-precedence studies in domestic fowl using genetic paternity assignment.

label: Insect larvae become motionless, egg-like stages before the adult emerges
claim: Insect larvae, after reaching full size, become a sort of egg: their outer husk hardens and they are motionless, as in bees, wasps and caterpillars.
quote: All these products that are of the nature of a scolex, after progressing and acquiring their full size, become a sort of egg, for the husk about them hardens and they are motionless during this period. This is plain in the scolex of bees and wasps and in caterpillars.
scope: insects with a larval ('scolex') stage: bees, wasps, butterflies and moths
measurable_quantities: presence of a non-feeding immobile pupal stage across insect orders
candidate_data: Life-cycle descriptions of holometabolous insects in the entomological literature and the Animal Diversity Web.

label: Some insects arise spontaneously in wool and water
claim: Some insects come into being without copulation, spontaneously, in wool and similar materials and in water.
quote: Similar to this is also what happens with all other insects which come into being without copulation in wool and other such materials and in water.
scope: insects such as clothes moths and aquatic insect larvae
measurable_quantities: emergence of insects from sterilised versus unsterilised substrates
candidate_data: Classic spontaneous-generation experiments (Redi, Spallanzani, Pasteur) and life-cycle records of clothes moths and aquatic insects.

label: Worker bees generate drones without copulation
claim: Worker bees produce drones without copulation, being female in generative power but containing both sexes as plants do.
quote: It remains then, as appears to be the case in certain fishes, that the bees should generate the drones without copulation, being indeed female in respect of generative power, but containing in themselves both sexes as plants do.
measurable_quantities: parentage of drones
production of drone brood by unmated workers
candidate_data: Honey-bee reproductive biology on arrhenotokous parthenogenesis and worker laying in queenless colonies.

label: Bee kings generate both kings and workers
claim: The 'kings' (leaders) of a hive generate both their own kind and the worker bees.
quote: since those occupied with the tendance of these creatures deny this, it remains that the kings must generate both their own kind and the bees.
scope: the honey bee (Apis mellifera); 'kings' are queens
measurable_quantities: maternity of workers and new queens in a colony
candidate_data: Honey-bee colony genetics and queen-rearing literature.

label: Fine seasons bring many drones, rainy seasons many workers
claim: In fine weather bees collect much honey and produce many drones, while in rainy seasons they produce a large brood of ordinary worker bees.
quote: Another fact is also natural, that in fine seasons much honey is collected and many drones are produced but in rainy reasons a large brood of ordinary bees.
measurable_quantities: drone-to-worker brood ratio by season and rainfall
honey yield
candidate_data: Apicultural colony monitoring data on brood composition and honey yield against weather records.

label: Observation must take precedence over theory
claim: Where the facts are sufficiently known, credit should be given to observation rather than to theories, and to theories only if they agree with the observed facts.
quote: the facts, however, have not yet been sufficiently grasped; if ever they are, then credit must be given rather to observation than to theories, and to theories only if what they affirm agrees with the observed facts.
candidate_data: none known

label: Few testaceans live on land, many in the sea
claim: Few or no kinds of testaceans (shelled molluscs and the like) live on land, snails being the exception, whereas in the sea there are many of every form.
quote: Because their nature answers to that of plants, therefore few or no kinds of testacea come into being on land, e.g. the snails and any others, few as they are, that resemble them; but in the sea and similar waters there are many of all kinds of forms.
measurable_quantities: number of shelled mollusc species by habitat (marine, freshwater, terrestrial)
candidate_data: Species counts by habitat from the World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS), MolluscaBase and GBIF.

label: Bloodless aquatic animals are rare in fresh water, common in estuaries
claim: Bloodless animals such as testaceans, cephalopods and crustaceans are not found in lakes or in the fresher brackish waters, except exceptionally, but arise in estuaries and at river mouths.
quote: Wherefore animals having no blood and not of a hot nature are not produced in lakes nor in the fresher among brackish waters, but only exceptionally, but it is in estuaries and at the mouths of rivers that they come into being, as testacea and cephalopoda and crustacea
scope: bloodless aquatic animals: testaceans, cephalopods, crustaceans
measurable_quantities: species richness and abundance of molluscs, cephalopods and crustaceans along salinity gradients
candidate_data: Occurrence records with habitat/salinity from GBIF and WoRMS environment flags (marine, brackish, freshwater).

label: Eels and some river fishes arise from scolex-like 'entrails of earth'
claim: Some blooded animals, including a kind of mullet, some other river fishes and the eels, arise without parents in scolex form; eels come into being in the so-called 'entrails of earth'.
quote: even some sanguinea, as a kind of mullet and some other river fishes and also the eel kind. For all of these, though they have but little blood by nature, are nevertheless sanguinea, and have a heart with blood in it as the origin of the parts; and the so-called ‘entrails of earth’, in which comes into being the body of the eel, have the nature of a scolex.
scope: eels (Anguilla), a kind of mullet and some river fishes
measurable_quantities: origin of eel recruits (spawning grounds, larval stages)
candidate_data: Life-cycle data for Anguilla anguilla (Sargasso Sea spawning, leptocephalus larvae) in FishBase and the eel-migration literature.

label: All testaceans arise spontaneously from putrefying mud
claim: All testaceans are formed spontaneously, for example on the sides of boats when frothy mud putrefies.
quote: That all the testacea are formed spontaneously is clear from such facts as these. They come into being on the side of boats when the frothy mud putrefies.
scope: testaceans (shelled molluscs, barnacles and the like)
measurable_quantities: presence of planktonic larvae and settlement on new substrates
reproduction by spawning
candidate_data: Larval biology and settlement studies of bivalves, gastropods and barnacles; reproductive data in SeaLifeBase.

label: Male and female twins often lie in the same part of the uterus
claim: Male and female twins are often found together in the same part of the uterus, in all viviparous animals, land animals and fish alike.
quote: Moreover male and female twins are often found together in the same part of the uterus; this we have observed sufficiently by dissection in all the vivipara, both land animals and fish.
measurable_quantities: sex of fetuses by uterine position in multiparous species
candidate_data: Intrauterine-position studies in rodents and pigs and fetal sex records from dissection studies.

label: Fish and serpents have no testes yet produce both sexes
claim: Fishes and serpents have no testes, yet they produce both male and female offspring, so the testes do not determine sex.
quote: a proof of this is that many animals in which the distinction of sex exists, and which produce both male and female offspring, nevertheless have no testes, as the footless animals; I mean the classes of fish and of serpents.
measurable_quantities: presence of testes in male fishes and snakes
candidate_data: Comparative gonad anatomy in Uberon/Phenoscape and the fish and reptile anatomy literature.

label: The male is what can concoct blood into form-bearing semen
claim: The male is defined as the sex able to concoct blood into semen that carries the principle of form; the female receives semen but cannot form or emit it.
quote: For the male is that which can concoct the blood into semen and which can form and secrete and discharge a semen carrying with it the principle of form
candidate_data: none known

label: Males are hotter than females
claim: Since concoction works by heat and the male concocts semen, the males of animals must be hotter than the females.
quote: And (2) all concoction works by means of heat. Therefore the males of animals must needs be hotter than the females.
scope: animals with separate sexes, especially those with blood
measurable_quantities: body temperature by sex
candidate_data: Sex-specific body-temperature measurements in mammals and birds from physiological datasets.

label: An embryo becomes female when the male principle fails for lack of heat
claim: An embryo becomes female when the male principle, through lack of heat, fails to master and concoct the material, which then changes into its opposite.
quote: For when the first principle does not bear sway and cannot concoct the nourishment through lack of heat nor bring it into its proper form, but is defeated in this respect, then must needs the material which it works on change into its opposite. Now the female is opposite to the male
measurable_quantities: offspring sex ratio under varied thermal or parental-condition regimes
candidate_data: Studies of sex determination mechanisms, including temperature-dependent sex determination in reptiles and fishes.

label: Young and ageing parents produce more females
claim: Parents who are young or approaching old age produce more female offspring than those in their prime.
quote: For more females are produced by the young and by those verging on old age than by those in the prime of life; in the former the vital heat is not yet perfect, in the latter it is failing.
measurable_quantities: offspring sex ratio by maternal and paternal age
candidate_data: National birth registries (e.g. US CDC natality data) with parental age and infant sex; livestock breeding records.

label: More males are conceived under north winds than south winds
claim: More males are born when copulation takes place while north winds blow than while south winds blow.
quote: Again, more males are born if copulation takes place when north than when south winds are blowing.
measurable_quantities: offspring sex ratio by wind direction at conception
candidate_data: Livestock breeding records with conception dates linked to historical meteorological wind data.

label: Menstruation naturally occurs when the moon is waning
claim: Menstruation naturally occurs more when the month (moon) is waning, that time being colder and moister.
quote: Also the fact that the catamenia occur in the course of nature rather when the month is waning is due to the same causes.
measurable_quantities: onset of menstruation by lunar phase
candidate_data: Large menstrual-cycle app datasets and published studies of menstrual onset against lunar phase.

label: Offspring resemble parents more than remoter ancestors
claim: Children resemble their parents more than their remoter ancestors, and those ancestors more than any chance individual.
quote: (2) They resemble their parents more than remoter ancestors, and resemble those ancestors more than any chance individual.
measurable_quantities: phenotypic similarity as a function of degree of relatedness
candidate_data: Twin and family studies of trait correlation by kinship degree; pedigree data in livestock breeding.

label: Unmastered paternal movements revert to those of the grandfather
claim: When the movement from the father in the semen is weakened ('resolved'), it changes into that of his father and then his grandfather, and likewise in the maternal line, so that children may resemble grandparents and remoter ancestors.
quote: for instance, if the movement of the male parent be resolved, it changes by a very slight difference into that of his father, and in the next instance into that of his grandfather; and in this way not only in the male but also in the female line the movement of the female parent changes into that of her mother
measurable_quantities: frequency of resemblance to grandparents versus parents for heritable traits
candidate_data: Multigenerational pedigree and genomic data (e.g. UK Biobank family relations) on trait resemblance.

label: Monstrosities are commonest in animals bearing many young, above all fowl
claim: Monstrosities are very rare in animals that bear one young, more frequent in those bearing many, and most frequent in birds, above all the domestic fowl.
quote: Hence also such monstrosities appear very rarely in animals producing only one young one, more frequently in those producing many, most of all in birds and among birds in the common fowl.
scope: animals generally; domestic fowl; humans compared with multiparous mammals
measurable_quantities: rate of congenital malformations or conjoined twinning by litter size across species
candidate_data: Veterinary and human congenital-anomaly registries (e.g. EUROCAT) and poultry hatchery malformation records.

label: Double-yolked eggs with fused yolks yield four-legged, four-winged chicks
claim: In double-yolked eggs, if the yolks are separated by a membrane two normal chicks result, but if the yolks are continuous the chick is monstrous, with one body and head but four legs and four wings.
quote: when the yolks are continuous, with no division between them, the chickens produced are monstrous, having one body and head but four legs and four wings
measurable_quantities: hatching outcomes and malformations from double-yolked eggs
candidate_data: Poultry embryology studies of double-yolked egg incubation and conjoined-twin chick reports.

label: No animal is born without a heart or wholly without a liver
claim: No animal has ever been born without a heart or entirely without a liver, though animals are born without a spleen, with two spleens or with one kidney.
quote: No animal, indeed, has ever been born without a heart, but they are born without a spleen or with two spleens or with one kidney; there is no case again of total absence of the liver, but there are cases of its being incomplete.
measurable_quantities: incidence of acardia, agenesis of liver, asplenia, polysplenia and renal agenesis
candidate_data: Human congenital-anomaly registries (EUROCAT) and veterinary teratology literature, including acardiac twin reports.

label: Hermaphrodite genitals occur in humans and especially in goats
claim: Animals are sometimes born with both male and female genitals; this occurs in humans and especially in goats.
quote: Again, they may have the generative parts doubled, the one being male, the other female; this is known in men and especially in goats.
measurable_quantities: incidence of intersex conditions in goats versus other livestock and humans
candidate_data: Veterinary genetics on intersexuality in goats (polled intersex syndrome) and human disorders-of-sex-development registries.

label: Large animals bear few young, small animals many
claim: Among walking, flying and swimming animals alike, large animals produce few young and small animals many, because in large animals the nutriment goes to increasing the body.
quote: And not only in animals that walk but also in those that fly or swim the large ones produce few, the small many, for the same reason.
scope: animals generally: mammals, birds and fishes
measurable_quantities: body mass
litter or clutch size
candidate_data: Body mass and litter/clutch size from PanTHERIA, the Amniote Life-History Database, AnAge and FishBase.

label: Human gestation alone is irregular, seven to ten months
claim: Man alone among animals has an irregular gestation period: children are born from seven to ten months, and eight-month children survive, though less often than the rest.
quote: On account of this it results that in man alone among animals the period of gestation is irregular; whereas the period is fixed in the rest, there are several periods in man, for children are born at seven months and at ten months and at the times between, for even those of eight months do live though less often than the rest.
measurable_quantities: variance in gestation length within species
survival by gestational age
candidate_data: Human birth registries with gestational age and survival; gestation-length variability in AnAge and veterinary data.

label: Women and mares alone accept the male during pregnancy
claim: Women and mares are the only animals that admit the male during gestation.
quote: therefore women and mares are the only animals which admit the male during gestation
measurable_quantities: occurrence of mating during pregnancy across mammal species
candidate_data: Behavioural studies of mating during pregnancy in primates, horses and other mammals.

label: Hares superfetate
claim: Superfetation (conceiving a second litter while already pregnant) occurs naturally in hares, because they are small, bear many young and are rich in semen.
quote: For superfoetation occurs in these animals, since they are not large and they bear many young (for they have many toes and the many-toed animals bear many), and they are spermatic.
measurable_quantities: frequency of superfetation in hares
candidate_data: Reproductive studies of the European brown hare (Lepus europaeus) documenting superfetation.

label: Hoofed animals bear young complete, most many-toed animals incomplete
claim: Among viviparous animals, solid-hoofed and cloven-footed animals bear their young fully formed, while most many-toed animals bear them imperfect (many born blind).
quote: Some of the vivipara produce their young imperfect, others perfect; the one-hoofed and cloven-footed perfect, most of the many-toed imperfect.
scope: viviparous quadrupeds: ungulates versus fissipeds (dog, wolf, fox, bear, lion), with the pig as exception
measurable_quantities: precocial versus altricial state at birth
eyes open at birth
foot type
candidate_data: Neonatal developmental state and litter size in PanTHERIA and the Amniote Life-History Database.

label: Young swallows' eyes regrow after being put out
claim: If the eyes of nestling swallows are put out, they recover their sight, because the birds are still developing and the eyes grow afresh.
quote: Hence if the eyes of swallows while still young be put out they recover their sight again, for the birds are still developing, not yet developed, when the injury is inflicted, so that the eyes grow and sprout afresh.
measurable_quantities: recovery of eye structure and vision after injury in nestlings
candidate_data: none known

label: In humans males are more often born defective than females
claim: In man, males are more often born defective than females, but this is not so in other animals.
quote: In man males are more often born defective than females, but in the other animals this is not the case.
measurable_quantities: congenital anomaly prevalence by sex in humans and in livestock
candidate_data: Human congenital-anomaly registries (EUROCAT) with sex-specific prevalence; veterinary malformation records.

label: Females develop slower in the womb but mature and age faster after birth
claim: In man the female develops more slowly than the male in the womb, but after birth reaches puberty, prime and old age sooner than the male.
quote: For while within the mother the female takes longer in developing, but after birth everything is perfected more quickly in females than in males; I mean, for instance, puberty, the prime of life, and old age.
measurable_quantities: fetal developmental rate by sex
age at puberty by sex
onset of senescence by sex
candidate_data: Fetal growth studies by sex, pubertal timing cohorts, and sex-specific ageing and mortality data (Human Mortality Database).

label: Nursing women neither menstruate nor conceive
claim: While women are suckling, menstruation naturally does not occur and they do not conceive; if they do conceive, the milk dries up, because milk and menses are the same secretion.
quote: While women are suckling children the catamenia do not occur according to Nature, nor do they conceive; if they do conceive, the milk dries up.
measurable_quantities: duration of lactational amenorrhoea
conception rate during breastfeeding
milk supply after conception
candidate_data: Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) breastfeeding and postpartum amenorrhoea data; clinical studies of lactational amenorrhoea.

label: All animals are naturally born head first
claim: The natural birth of all animals is head first, because the parts above the umbilical cord are larger and heavier.
quote: The natural birth of all animals is head-foremost, because the parts above the umbilical cord are larger than those below.
measurable_quantities: fetal presentation at birth across mammal species
candidate_data: Obstetric records of fetal presentation in humans and veterinary data on birth presentation in livestock and cetaceans.

label: Gestation length is caused by the size of the offspring, not by lifespan
claim: Gestation length roughly corresponds to lifespan only incidentally; its real cause is the size of the offspring, since large masses take long to perfect.
quote: but the cause of the time of gestation is the size of the offspring. For it is not easy for large masses to arrive at their perfection in a small time
measurable_quantities: gestation length
neonatal mass
maximum lifespan
candidate_data: Gestation length, neonatal mass and maximum longevity in AnAge and PanTHERIA.

label: Horses gestate a year, humans ten months, elephants two years
claim: Horses and their kin carry their young for a year, man at most ten months, and elephants for two years.
quote: That is why horses and animals akin to them, though living a shorter time than man, yet carry their young longer; for the time in the former is a year, but in the latter ten months at the outside. For the same reason also the time is long in elephants; they carry their young two years on account of their excessive size.
scope: horse, ass and kin (Equus), humans, elephants
measurable_quantities: gestation length in Equus, Homo sapiens and Elephantidae
candidate_data: Gestation lengths in AnAge and PanTHERIA.

label: Man lives longer than any animal except the elephant
claim: Man lives longer than any animal for which there is credible evidence, except the elephant.
quote: Man lives a longer time than any animal of which we have any credible experience except the elephant
scope: humans compared with other animals, especially mammals
measurable_quantities: maximum recorded lifespan across species
candidate_data: Maximum longevity records in AnAge.

label: Eye colour has no final cause unless characteristic of the kind
claim: Features not characteristic of a whole kind, such as an individual's eye colour, do not exist for a final cause but arise of necessity from the material and the efficient cause.
quote: The eye for instance exists for a final cause, but it is not blue for a final cause unless this condition be characteristic of the kind of animal.
scope: variable traits of animals, especially in man
candidate_data: none known

label: Embryos sleep most of the time but wake briefly in the womb
claim: Embryos sleep most of the time, though they are found to wake briefly even in the womb, which is why newborns spend most of their time asleep.
quote: But nevertheless they are found to wake even in the womb (this is clear in dissections and in the ovipara), and then they immediately fall into a sleep again. This is why after birth also they spend most of their time in sleep.
scope: animal embryos and newborns, including humans
measurable_quantities: fetal sleep-wake states
proportion of time newborns spend asleep
candidate_data: Fetal behavioural-state studies by ultrasound and neonatal sleep polysomnography data.

label: Infants laugh only in sleep, not awake
claim: Infants do not laugh when awake, but while asleep they both laugh and cry.
quote: When awake infants do not laugh, but while asleep they both laugh and cry.
measurable_quantities: age at onset of waking social laughter
smiling and crying during sleep
candidate_data: Developmental studies of neonatal smiling and laughter onset.

label: All newborn children have bluish eyes that later change colour
claim: The eyes of all children are bluish at birth and later change to their permanent colour, which is not seen in other animals.
quote: The eyes of all children are bluish immediately after birth; later on they change to the colour which is to be theirs permanently. But in the case of other animals this is not visible.
measurable_quantities: iris colour at birth and in later infancy across populations
candidate_data: Studies of newborn iris colour across ethnic populations and longitudinal infant eye-colour change.

label: Only horses and humans have eyes of different colours
claim: Of animals other than man, the horse has the greatest variety of eye colour and some horses have two differently coloured eyes; this is seen in no other animal, but sometimes in man.
quote: Of the other animals the horse has the greatest variety of colour in the eye, for some of them are actually heteroglaucous; this phenomenon is not to be seen in any of the other animals, but man is sometimes heteroglaucous.
measurable_quantities: occurrence of heterochromia iridum across species
candidate_data: Veterinary records of heterochromia in horses, dogs and cats; Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals (OMIA).

label: Blue eyes see poorly by day, dark eyes poorly by night
claim: Blue eyes are not keen-sighted by day and dark eyes are not keen-sighted by night.
quote: We must suppose the same cause also to be responsible for the fact that blue eyes are not keen-sighted by day nor dark eyes by night.
measurable_quantities: visual acuity and glare sensitivity in bright light by iris colour
scotopic vision by iris colour
candidate_data: Ophthalmological studies of iris pigmentation and glare, contrast sensitivity and dark adaptation.

label: Cataract attacks blue eyes more, night-blindness dark eyes
claim: Cataract affects blue-eyed people more, while nyctalopia affects dark-eyed people more.
quote: Cataract attacks the blue-eyed more, but what is called ‘nyctalopia’ the dark-eyed.
measurable_quantities: cataract incidence by iris colour
night-blindness incidence by iris colour
candidate_data: Epidemiological studies of cataract risk by iris colour (e.g. UK Biobank ophthalmic data).

label: Animals with deep-set eyes see far, those with prominent eyes do not
claim: Animals with prominent eyes do not see well at a distance, whereas those whose eyes lie deep in the head can see distant things.
quote: A proof of this is that animals with prominent eyes do not see well at a distance, whereas those which have their eyes lying deep in the head can see things at a distance
measurable_quantities: eye protrusion or orbital depth
visual acuity at distance
candidate_data: Comparative visual acuity compilations for vertebrates combined with skull and orbit morphometrics (e.g. MorphoSource specimens).

label: The seal has no external ears, only hearing passages
claim: The seal, though a viviparous quadruped, has no external ears but only passages for hearing, because it lives in the water.
quote: The workmanship of Nature is admirable also in the seal, for though a viviparous quadruped it has no ears but only passages for hearing. This is because its life is passed in the water
measurable_quantities: presence of external pinnae in pinnipeds
candidate_data: Pinniped anatomy in the Animal Diversity Web and Phenoscape/Uberon anatomy annotations.

label: Men go bald in front and grey first at the temples
claim: Men go bald on the front of the head but turn grey first on the temples; no one goes bald first on the temples or the back of the head.
quote: Men go bald on the front of the head, but turn grey first on the temples; no one goes bald first on these or on the back of the head.
measurable_quantities: scalp region of first hair loss
scalp region of first greying
candidate_data: Dermatological studies of androgenetic alopecia patterns (Hamilton–Norwood scale) and greying onset by scalp region.

label: Only humans visibly go grey with age, and to a lesser degree horses
claim: Humans go grey on the head as they age, but this is not visible in practically any other animal except, to some extent, the horse.
quote: Human beings also go grey on the head as they grow old, but this is not visible in practically any other animal, though more so in the horse than others.
measurable_quantities: age-related greying across mammal species
candidate_data: Studies of age-related greying in dogs, horses, primates and other mammals.

label: Peoples of moist cold lands are straight-haired, of hot dry lands curly
claim: Peoples living in moist air, such as the Scythians and Thracians, are straight-haired, while Ethiopians and others in hot countries are curly-haired because their brains and the surrounding air are dry.
quote: For this reason the Scythians on the Black Sea and the Thracians are straight-haired, for both they themselves and the environing air are moist, whereas the Aethiopians and men in hot countries are curly-haired, for their brains and the surrounding air are dry.
measurable_quantities: hair curvature across human populations
climate (temperature, humidity) of ancestral regions
candidate_data: Anthropometric studies of hair form across populations combined with climate data.

label: Deep-water sea-urchins have large, hard spines because of cold
claim: Sea-urchins that live in deep, cold water (sixty fathoms or more) have large, hard spines though their bodies are small.
quote: For these, too, though small themselves, have large and hard spines because the sea in which they live is cold on account of its depth (for they are found in sixty fathoms and even more).
measurable_quantities: spine length relative to test diameter by depth
water temperature
candidate_data: Echinoid occurrence and depth records in GBIF and OBIS with morphometric data from museum collections.

label: Women and eunuchs do not go bald
claim: Women do not go bald, since like children they produce no seminal secretion, and eunuchs do not go bald because they change into the female condition.
quote: Women do not go bald because their nature is like that of children, both alike being incapable of producing seminal secretion. Eunuchs do not become bald, because they change into the female condition.
measurable_quantities: incidence of pattern baldness in women and in men castrated before puberty
candidate_data: Clinical studies of androgenetic alopecia in castrated men and in women.

label: Hair covered by hats goes grey sooner
claim: Greying is a kind of decay, so hair protected by hats or other coverings, being sheltered from the winds, goes grey sooner.
quote: hair protected by hats or other coverings goes grey sooner (for the winds prevent decay and the protection keeps off the winds)
measurable_quantities: age at greying in habitual hat-wearers versus non-wearers
candidate_data: none known

label: White individuals occur in normally uniform-coloured species
claim: Even in uniformly coloured kinds, white individuals occasionally arise when development is perverted, as has been seen in partridges, ravens, sparrows and bears.
quote: but still they do so change, for before now white individuals have been observed among partridges, ravens, sparrows, and bears.
scope: partridges, ravens, sparrows, bears and other uniformly coloured animals
measurable_quantities: frequency of albino or leucistic individuals
candidate_data: Records of albinism and leucism in birds and mammals, including GBIF occurrence notes and OMIA.

label: Hot drinking water whitens hair, cold water darkens it
claim: Colour change in animals whose kind is many-coloured is due to the water they drink: hot waters make the hair white and cold waters make it dark.
quote: This is owing to the water which they drink, for hot waters make the hair white, cold makes it dark, an effect found also in plants.
scope: animals whose individuals are whole-coloured but whose kind is many-coloured (e.g. cattle, goats)
measurable_quantities: coat colour of offspring against drinking-water temperature
candidate_data: none known

label: The belly is whiter in animals that are not uniformly coloured
claim: In all animals that are not uniformly coloured, the underside of the belly is whiter.
quote: Hence also in all animals not uniformly coloured all the part under the belly is whiter.
measurable_quantities: dorsal versus ventral coloration across species
candidate_data: Comparative studies of countershading in mammals, birds and fishes; museum specimen colour data.

label: Females have higher voices than males, except in cattle
claim: In animals generally the female's voice is higher than the male's, most plainly in man, but in cattle the cow's voice is deeper than the bull's.
quote: in the other kinds of animals the voice of the female is higher than that of the male (this being especially plain in man, for Nature has given this faculty to him in the highest degree because he alone of animals makes use of speech and the voice is the material of speech), but in cattle the opposite obtains, for the voice of cows is deeper than that of bulls.
measurable_quantities: fundamental frequency of vocalisations by sex
bull versus cow call pitch
candidate_data: Bioacoustic recordings (e.g. Macaulay Library, xeno-canto) and published acoustic analyses of cattle vocalisations by sex.

label: A bone is found in the heart of some bulls
claim: A bone is found in the heart of some bulls.
quote: That the heart of bulls is of such a nature is shown by the fact that a bone is actually found in some of them
measurable_quantities: presence of an os cordis in bovine hearts
candidate_data: Veterinary anatomy of the bovine os cordis; Uberon anatomy annotations.

label: Castrated animals take on a female voice and character
claim: All animals, when castrated, change to the female character and utter a voice like that of females.
quote: All animals when castrated change to the female character, and utter a voice like that of the females because the sinewy strength in the principle of the voice is relaxed.
scope: male animals with testes, including humans
measurable_quantities: vocal pitch and secondary sexual characters after castration
candidate_data: Studies of castrated livestock and of castrati and androgen effects on vocal-fold development.

label: The pig does not shed its teeth; lions shed only their canines
claim: The pig does not shed its teeth, and some carnivores, such as lions, shed no teeth except the canines.
quote: Yet the pig also suckles but does not shed its teeth, and, further, all the animals with carnivorous dentition suckle, but some of them do not shed any teeth except the canines, e.g. lions.
scope: pigs and carnivores such as lions
measurable_quantities: presence and replacement of deciduous teeth in Sus and Panthera
candidate_data: Mammalian dental-eruption and replacement data in the zoological and veterinary literature.

label: Nature never fails nor does anything in vain
claim: Nature never fails nor does anything in vain, so far as is possible in each case.
quote: Now we assume, basing our assumption upon what we see, that Nature never fails nor does anything in vain so far as is possible in each case.
candidate_data: none known

label: The last human grinders erupt around age twenty
claim: The grinding teeth keep growing for a long time, the last of them cutting the gum at about twenty years of age and sometimes in old age.
quote: A proof of this is that even the flat teeth grow for a long time, the last of them cutting the gum at about twenty years of age; indeed in some cases the last teeth have been grown in quite old age.
measurable_quantities: age at eruption of third molars
candidate_data: Dental-eruption reference data for third molars from clinical and forensic odontology studies.

label: Young fed hotter milk cut their teeth sooner
claim: Suckling itself does not form the teeth, but the heat of the milk speeds them: young that receive hotter milk grow their teeth more quickly.
quote: A proof of this is that even in suckling animals those young which enjoy hotter milk grow their teeth quicker, heat being conducive to growth.
measurable_quantities: age at tooth eruption against milk temperature or composition
candidate_data: none known
